name: Torsemide
sections: White to off-white crystalline powder, practically insoluble in water.

The TRANSFORM-HF trial (2023) found no mortality difference versus furosemide in heart failure, but torsemide offers more predictable absorption and longer action. First approval/introduction: Patented 1974; introduced 1993 (Boehringer Mannheim).

Inhibits the Na+/K+/2Cl- co-transporter in the thick ascending loop of Henle, causing natriuresis and diuresis; also mild anti-aldosterone effect and reduction of myocardial fibrosis. Receptor / target profile: Inhibits the Na+/K+/2Cl− co-transporter in the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle; also has anti-aldosterone and anti-fibrotic effects.
Summary: Bioavailability ~80–90% (more predictable than furosemide); Tmax ~1 h. >99% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP2C9. Half-life ~3.5 h (diuretic effect 6–8 h).
Oedema associated with congestive heart failure, renal disease (including nephrotic syndrome) and hepatic cirrhosis
Heart failure oedema: 10–20 mg once daily; titrate (doubling) up to 200 mg
Chronic kidney disease: 20 mg once daily, titrate up to 200 mg
Hepatic cirrhosis: 5–10 mg once daily with an aldosterone antagonist
Hypertension: 2.5–5 mg once daily, up to 10 mg
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Effective even in advanced CKD; higher doses may be needed.
Cirrhosis: start low with aldosterone antagonist; risk of hepatic coma with electrolyte shifts.
Start low; dehydration and falls risk.

With or without food; take in the morning.
Electrolytes (Na, K, Mg), creatinine, uric acid, glucose; weight and fluid status.

TORIC (Cosín et al., 2002) – torsemide associated with lower mortality than furosemide/other diuretics (observational).

Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
